In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the R-M-S system is an ancient system that is still being used by bacteria to protect themselves against invading DNA.
bifunctional enzymes are not only a result of a gene fusion but are also a product of a natural selection.
the bifunctional endo- and methyltransferase enzymes are not a rare case, but are a widespread group of restriction enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new bifunctional enzyme, which is isoschizome of a known restriction-modification system.

the bifunctional restriction enzyme AloI is a fusion of a restriction nuklease and a DNA-methyl-transferase, which is able to cleave the DNA in a Mg-dependent manner and is an isoschizomerase of AloI.
we have found a new bifunctional restriction endonuclease and methyltransferase enzyme, PcoI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of potential bifunctional enzymes is growing and the majority of them are fusions of type I R-M-S subunit and type IIC restriction endonuclease.
the phylogenetic tree analysis of restriction endonucleasemethyltransferases can be used for prediction of new bifunctional enzymes and for their further study.
bifunctional endo-methylase enzymes can be successfully used in genetic engineering.
